filename: Stress-testing the coupled behavior of hybrid physics-machine learning climate simulations on an unseen, warmer climate.pdf
title: Stress-testing the coupled behavior of hybrid physics-machine learning climate simulations on an unseen, warmer climate
parameterization_target: subgrid convection and radiation (heating and moistening tendencies)
testbed_rationale: The simulation datasets and code are not explicitly provided with a public URL, DOI, or repository link in the text.
pain_points: Unstable coupled simulations (premature simulation termination in online coupled testing, only 4.5% to 23% completed a full year)
Poor out-of-distribution generalization in warmer climates (+4K SST), where uncoupled errors spike and baseline models fail
Coupled moisture errors are consistently worse in out-of-distribution climates than in-distribution
Models performing best in one climate do not necessarily perform best in another
Current single-climate architectural adjustments (climate-invariant features, expanded inputs, memory) do not preclude the need for multi-climate training data
extraction_notes: The study tests ML parameterizations coupled into SPCAM 3 using Fortran-Keras Bridge (FKB) across 330 neural network configurations under control and +4K warm climate conditions.
